metaDesc: A real 3-day, 2-night Phrae itinerary in northern Thailand: old town and Wat Phra That Cho Hae, the Phae Mueang Phi earth pillars, then Wiang Kosai and Mae Koeng Waterfall, with timings, eats, and entry fees.
keywords: Phrae itinerary, Phrae 3 days 2 nights, Phae Mueang Phi, Wiang Kosai, Mae Koeng Waterfall, Wat Phra That Cho Hae
h1:
Phrae 3 Days 2 Nights
Old Town · Phae Mueang Phi · Wiang Kosai
intro: Phrae is one of those quieter provinces you can take slowly without feeling like you're missing out. It has old teakwood houses, Burmese-style temples, indigo-dyed mo hom cloth, and patches of nature within an easy drive of town. This plan runs three days and two nights: day one eases through the old town and pays respects at Wat Phra That Cho Hae, day two heads out to the Phae Mueang Phi earth pillars and the mo hom weaving street, and the last day is all nature at Wiang Kosai National Park and Mae Koeng Waterfall before you leave.

blocks.html: Plenty of people drive straight through Phrae on the way to Nan, even though the town itself has more to see than you'd expect. Three days and two nights is about right here, unhurried, with room for the old town, local food, and the nature outside the city. This plan is built around places that are actually open and distances you can comfortably drive each day. Feel free to shuffle the days around the weather, especially the day you head up to Wiang Kosai. If it's pouring, push it back or swap it with an old-town day.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Phrae is easiest with your own car or a rental, since the sights are spread out around the edges of town. That's especially true on day three, when you head out to Wang Chin district, which sits a fair distance from the city center. If you don't have a vehicle, your best bet is to hire a local car by the day.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Phrae Old Town + Wat Phra That Cho Hae

blocks.html: Day one covers everything in and around town. Start inside the old city walls, walking past teakwood houses and old temples, then drive up to Wat Phra That Cho Hae in the afternoon, the province's principal stupa, before coming back for dinner in town.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Ease through the old town, pay respects at the town's stupa

items.activity: Start the morning with khanom jeen nam ngiao
items.note: There are several old khanom jeen shops in town, like Pa Jit, serving nam ngiao, pork broth, and nam ya from around THB 20 a bowl. It's a proper Phrae-style breakfast.

items.activity: Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang Worawihan
items.note: The town's main royal temple, open roughly 08:30-17:00. Walk through the ordination hall and the temple museum. It sits near Khum Chao Luang, so you can carry on by foot.

items.activity: Khum Chao Luang (the old governor's residence)
items.note: A teakwood mansion in gingerbread style, blending Thai and European influences, raised about 2 meters off the ground with as many as 72 doors and windows. Open daily around 08:30-16:30, and one of the town's standout photo spots.
A century-old pink teakwood house belonging to an old ruling family, with finely carved fretwork and a collection on display inside. It's a short walk from Khum Chao Luang.
The walled quarter has several cafes set in old wooden houses, including ones with gardens out back. A good place to duck out of the afternoon sun before heading out of town.

Phrae's principal stupa, an octagonal Chiang Saen-style chedi standing about 33 meters tall on a low hill, around 9 km from town. Locals say that coming to Phrae without paying respects at Cho Hae is like never really arriving.
The only surviving Burmese Bagan-style temple in Phrae, registered as a historic monument. The woodwork and fretwork are lovely, and it catches the late-afternoon light well.

Pick a northern Thai restaurant or a mookata spot in town. If you happen to be here on a walking-street night (Kad Sam Wai / Kad Kong Kao on Saturday evenings), you can graze on local food for a good while.

blocks.title: Make the most of the old town on foot
blocks.html: Khum Chao Luang, Ban Wongburi, and Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang are all within walking distance of one another inside the old city walls. Park once and walk between them to save both time and the hassle of parking.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Phae Mueang Phi + Mo Hom Weaving at Ban Thung Hong

blocks.html: Day two heads out of town to the north. The morning, while it's still cool, is good for Phae Mueang Phi and its oddly shaped earth pillars, followed by Ban Thung Hong, the town's home of mo hom cloth. Later in the afternoon, take in a big teakwood house and pick up some souvenirs before heading back.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: The Phae Mueang Phi earth pillars + local mo hom cloth

items.note: Fuel up with sticky rice and sai ua, kaep mu, or a coffee from a morning shop before driving to Phae Mueang Phi, about 8 km from town. Going early means the sun isn't too harsh yet.

Earth pillars and eroded clay cliffs in strange shapes, carved out naturally over time. There's a loop trail to walk, and entry runs in the tens of baht. Wear comfortable walking shoes, as some stretches are sandy.

items.activity: Ban Thung Hong — the mo hom street
items.note: A village that makes traditional indigo-dyed mo hom cloth, with shops lining both sides of the road for several kilometers. Browse mo hom clothing here; there's no entry fee, and some shops let you try dyeing a piece yourself.
There are northern Thai restaurants and local noodle shops in the area. Grab a bite to tide you over before the afternoon.
A large teakwood house built using more than a hundred whole teak posts. Open daily around 08:00-17:00, entry about THB 15. A relaxed walk-through of the woodwork and collections.

items.activity: Souvenir shopping on the way back into town
items.note: Pick up Phrae's well-known treats like khao kaep crackers, sai ua, and kaep mu, plus mo hom shirts, before heading back into town.
Choose a restaurant with a nice atmosphere in town, or a cafe that stays open into the evening. Wind down before tomorrow's longer drive.

items.name: Ban Thung Hong mo hom cloth
items.blurb: Phrae's signature buy: deep-blue indigo-dyed cotton you can actually wear, whether as a shirt or a scarf. Prices start in the low hundreds of baht.

items.name: Khao kaep & kaep mu
items.blurb: Local snacks that are easy to take home and keep well, making them a handy souvenir to grab on your way out.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Wiang Kosai + Mae Koeng Waterfall

blocks.html: The last day is a nature day. Drive out toward Wang Chin district to head up Wiang Kosai National Park and Mae Koeng Waterfall. It's a fair distance from town, around 1.5-2 hours of driving depending on the route, so set off a little early to have time at the waterfall and make it back before dark.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: The green forest of Wiang Kosai, a 7-tier waterfall

items.note: It's a long drive today, so eat early and fill up the tank before leaving town, since gas stations around Wang Chin are spread out.

items.activity: Set off for Wang Chin district
items.note: Take Highway 1023 (Phrae-Wang Chin) through Long district. The views along the way are mountains and farmland, an easy 1.5-2 hour drive.

items.activity: Arrive at Wiang Kosai National Park
items.note: A green forest park rated highly for its environmental standards, with cool, comfortable air. Stop at the headquarters to ask about the trails and pay the entry fee before walking to the waterfall.

A tiered waterfall of around 7 levels. It's about a 1 km walk from the parking area to the lowest tier, with roughly another 200 meters between tiers 1 and 7. The water is clear, and you can swim in the safe sections. It looks its best in late rainy season into early winter.
There are rest areas and food stalls near the headquarters, or you can bring a packed lunch and picnic by the water for the atmosphere.

items.activity: Short hike / take in the view
items.note: If you've still got the energy, walk one of the short nature trails around the headquarters, or take in the green forest before packing up to head back.

items.activity: Drive back to town / on to your next stop
items.note: Drive back into Phrae town to catch your ride home, or carry on to Den Chai to catch a train or head to another province. Leave enough buffer to arrive before dark.

blocks.title: About Mae Koeng Waterfall
blocks.html: The waterfall is at its best, with plenty of water, from late rainy season into early winter. In the dry season the flow can be thin. If you come during the rains, watch for slippery paths and always check conditions with the park headquarters before getting in the water.

items: 2 nights' lodging — hotels and guesthouses in Phrae town start around THB 500-1,200 per night.

Entry fees — Baan Prathup Jai about THB 15 · Phae Mueang Phi in the tens of baht · Wiang Kosai has an entry fee at the standard national park rate, adding up to only a few hundred baht for the whole trip.
Food — local meals start at THB 20-60 each, so the whole trip is easy on the wallet.
Car / fuel — depends on your vehicle and where you start. Day three out to Wang Chin uses the most fuel, so budget a little extra for that leg.

faq.q: Do I need my own car for a 3-day, 2-night Phrae trip?
faq.a: It's easiest with your own car or a rental, since the sights are spread out around town. That's especially true on day three out to Wiang Kosai National Park in Wang Chin district, which is far and has little public transport. If you don't have a vehicle, hiring a local car by the day works well. The old-town day, on the other hand, is easy enough to do on foot.

faq.q: Are Phae Mueang Phi and Mae Koeng Waterfall close together? Can I do both in one day?
faq.a: They're in different directions and far apart. Phae Mueang Phi is about 8 km north of town, while Mae Koeng Waterfall is in Wiang Kosai National Park in Wang Chin district, around 1.5-2 hours' drive from the city. So it's best to split them across separate days as in this plan, to avoid wearing yourself out and to leave enough time.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Phrae?
faq.a: Late rainy season into winter (roughly November to February) is best: the air is cool and comfortable, the old town isn't too hot to walk, and Mae Koeng Waterfall is full and looking its best. In the dry season the waterfall can run thin.

faq.q: What souvenirs from Phrae should I take home?
faq.a: Mo hom cloth from Ban Thung Hong is the signature buy, and it's genuinely wearable as both shirts and scarves. For food, there's khao kaep, kaep mu, and sai ua, which keep well and make handy souvenirs to grab on your way out.

faq.q: Is Wat Phra That Cho Hae far from town?
faq.a: Not far, about 9 km from Phrae town, just a few minutes' drive. It's the province's principal stupa, and locals consider a visit a must when you come to Phrae. It slots neatly into the afternoon of day one.
